page: The Microsoft Azure D2ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine provisioned on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at clock speeds up to 4.2 GHz. The configuration allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs executed across 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. System memory totals 8.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture features an integrated 118 GB local NVMe SSD for high-throughput ephemeral caching. The instance does not include a dedicated GPU. Architectural instruction extensions include Intel AMX (amx_tile, amx_int8), AVX-512, and cryptographic acceleration through AES and VAES.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate solid single-threaded responsiveness alongside predictable multi-core scaling limitations. In single-core evaluations, the server achieves average percentiles, recording a stress-ng score of 1937.79 and a Geekbench single-core result of 1661.0. For targeted vector execution, small-model (135M) LLM text generation achieved 119.14 tokens per second. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics reflect the two-vCPU scale, with stress-ng multi-core (1991.89) and Geekbench multi-core (2015.0) scoring in the lower benchmark tier. Similarly, memory bandwidth reaches 154.85 GB/sec for small cached blocks but scales down to 20.87 GB/sec for uncached read streams, resulting in restrained compiler build rates (2128.0 in Clang) and moderate static web serving throughput of 4.31 GB/sec.

From a resource economics standpoint, the D2ds_v6 delivers solid density by bundling high-speed local NVMe storage with modern Intel Xeon computing power, avoiding the immediate need for auxiliary managed storage for scratch data. The primary architectural tradeoff is limited core concurrency and constrained memory bandwidth under parallel load, which makes the instance unsuitable for large-scale data ingestion or high-concurrency database clusters. However, the balance of single-thread agility, hardware encryption, and integrated NVMe capacity positions the instance effectively for lightweight web serving, containerized microservices, development pipelines, and distributed Redis worker nodes.
description: Microsoft Azure D2ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance allocates two dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyper-threading at frequencies reaching 4.2 GHz, supported by 8 GB of memory and a bundled 118 GB local NVMe solid-state drive. Hardware feature support includes advanced vector and matrix instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AMX. Benchmark results highlight reliable single-thread capabilities with average performance in Geekbench and stress-ng tests, alongside acceptable small-model LLM token generation. However, multi-core throughput and raw memory bandwidth are constrained due to the two-vCPU hardware footprint, placing multi-threaded compile and compute tests in lower benchmark percentiles. The inclusion of high-speed local NVMe storage provides strong I/O efficiency without external disk overhead, making D2ds_v6 well suited for microservices, lightweight web servers, development environments, and small-scale caching layers.
